beats.visual: Soft graphite storybook close-up of the Red Horned Everyman's eyes in three-quarter profile as he notices another person's mouth opening into a yawn at the opposite edge of the cream-paper scene; a faint pencil sightline leads from his gaze to the stretching jaw.
beats.purpose: show the initial visual detection of another person's yawn
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme close-up of host eyes plus another person's yawning jaw, diagonal gaze line, shallow workshop-neutral background, eye-to-mouth composition
beats.continuity: begins the body with the host observing a nearby human action, but isolates only the eye-to-jaw cue

beats.narration_slice: The brain recognizes a familiar human action.
beats.visual: A simple graphite anatomical silhouette of a human head seen from the side, with a softly shaded brain shape containing a tiny ghosted pencil sketch of a yawning face, suggesting recognition rather than literal brain detail.
beats.purpose: show the brain identifying the observed movement as a familiar human action
beats.visual_fingerprint: side-profile head diagram, centered brain silhouette, miniature yawning-face memory echo, clean cream-paper field, no host
beats.continuity: moves inward from the observed face to an intuitive internal recognition diagram

beats.visual: Overhead storybook view of a small social scene where several muted figures and objects remain softly unfinished while one yawning person is sharply emphasized by converging graphite strokes and the host's head turning toward them.
beats.purpose: show attention rapidly reorienting toward the yawn
beats.visual_fingerprint: high overhead angle, small group scene, host pivoting head, converging pencil emphasis on one yawner, peripheral details fading unfinished
beats.continuity: returns from the internal diagram to the social scene with a new overhead composition focused on attentional shift

beats.narration_slice: Perception and movement systems may prime a matching response.
beats.visual: Split-free conceptual pencil illustration of a seated human figure with one faint graphite echo tracing from an observed yawning face near the head toward a second ghosted jaw-opening pose in the figure's own body, linked by soft curved motion strokes.
beats.purpose: show perception and movement systems becoming prepared for a similar action
beats.visual_fingerprint: single seated figure, ghosted observed face above-left, matching jaw-motion echo below-right, curved pencil pathway, sparse conceptual setting
beats.continuity: abstracts the attention shift into a restrained perception-to-movement pathway without reusing the prior group scene

beats.narration_slice: That can make your own yawn easier to trigger.
beats.visual: Medium side view of the Red Horned Everyman seated alone at a plain table, lips beginning to part and one hand hovering near his mouth as a barely visible graphite motion echo suggests the yawn is just starting.
beats.purpose: show the observer becoming more likely to yawn himself
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium side profile of host at table, restrained pre-yawn mouth opening, hovering hand, isolated domestic-neutral setting, horizontal negative space behind him
beats.continuity: translates the priming concept into the host's own subtle physical response in a fresh side-view setting

beats.visual: Three people arranged in a loose diagonal across the cream paper, the first fully yawning, the second beginning to open their mouth, and the third just reacting with widened eyes; soft graphite echo-arcs imply the behavior passing along without any labels.
beats.purpose: show the phenomenon of one yawn spreading to another person
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-person diagonal chain, sequential yawn stages, no host, open cream background, repeated arc motif connecting faces
beats.continuity: widens from one individual's response to a small human chain that makes the contagious effect visually obvious

beats.narration_slice: It occurs in humans and some social animals.
beats.visual: Gentle storybook scene with a yawning human seated on a low park bench while, several feet away, a non-specific social primate and a domestic dog are each shown in separate natural poses with open mouths suggesting yawns, surrounded by sparse sage foliage.
beats.purpose: show that contagious-yawn-like behavior has been observed in humans and some social animals
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide outdoor park vignette, human on bench plus primate and dog at different depths, muted foliage, triangular composition, no host
beats.continuity: expands the concept beyond the prior all-human chain by moving outdoors and introducing social animals

beats.narration_slice: Social connection may influence who catches it.
beats.visual: Two close friends lean toward each other on one side of the frame while two unfamiliar figures remain more distant on the other; a soft pencil ripple from a yawn reaches the close pair clearly but fades before the distant pair.
beats.purpose: show that social closeness may affect transmission of a yawn
beats.visual_fingerprint: paired intimate foreground figures versus distant background strangers, fading ripple motif, asymmetric depth composition, quiet indoor social setting
beats.continuity: shifts from species breadth to relationship strength using spatial closeness rather than repeating the previous animal scene

beats.narration_slice: But the exact mechanism remains unsettled.
beats.visual: A restrained graphite research-table still life with overlapping sketches of an eye, brain, jaw, and small human silhouettes connected by several incomplete dotted pencil paths that trail off into unfinished construction marks.
beats.purpose: show that scientists do not yet have one settled mechanism explaining the effect
beats.visual_fingerprint: top-down research-table composition, scattered anatomical sketches, incomplete branching pathways, worn paper scraps, no people present
beats.continuity: moves from social-pattern imagery to an intentionally unresolved explanatory diagram with incomplete connections

beats.narration_slice: Evidence tying it directly to empathy is mixed.
beats.visual: Balanced pencil metaphor of two simple human silhouettes facing a yawning figure: one silhouette has a warm muted brick-red thread-like connection toward the yawner while the other has a broken, fading thread, both surrounded by ambiguous graphite marks rather than symbols or text.
beats.purpose: show that research linking contagious yawning directly to empathy gives inconsistent results
beats.visual_fingerprint: frontal trio of silhouettes, one continuous warm connection and one broken fading connection, centered yawner, symmetrical cream-paper composition
beats.continuity: narrows the unresolved mechanism question to the specific empathy hypothesis using contrasting intact and broken social links

beats.narration_slice: So seeing a yawn can quietly set another in motion.
beats.visual: Return to the Red Horned Everyman in a calm three-quarter medium shot as someone in the soft-focus background yawns; the host's expression shifts from skeptical observation to the first involuntary opening of his own mouth, with a subtle graphite motion echo connecting the two actions.
beats.purpose: summarize the chain from seeing another person's yawn to beginning one yourself
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-quarter medium host foreground, blurred background yawner, delayed mirrored mouth opening, gentle diagonal motion echo, quiet neutral room
beats.continuity: returns to the host for the explanatory payoff while using a new foreground-background composition distinct from his earlier close-up and side profile
